steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: We meet again so soon, DisCity native. Right... everyone here is.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: What do they call you? Chief? Is that a high rank?
You don't need to be so defensive. I do trust you.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hah. So this is your "trust"?

The simple addition of a remote observer watching through cameras transforms the familiar interrogation room into something alien. A blast of cold air sweeps through as Ceto sits with a defiant posture, her arms bound by metal restraints threaded through leather.

These extreme security measures are a perfect embodiment of the fear and wariness DisCity's leadership holds for "Rancors"—an attitude Ceto has clearly internalized. It is no wonder, then, that her every word drips with sarcasm.
These are... precautions. Sinner interrogations are normally handled by the MBCC alone, but this case is an exception. I'll be honest with you; our conversation is being monitored by several guests.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: A moment, Chief. Revealing such operational details to the suspect... is that your considered judgment? I fail to see the benefit.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: So your "guests" have a voice, too. And here I was, almost believing you. Turns out your word doesn't mean much.

Ceto's enhanced hearing, a common trait among Sinners, leaves no syllable of your internal dispute a secret. The derisive snort she lets out is a clear and mocking judgment on the ridiculousness of your team's discord.
It is my decision. I am directly responsible for this interrogation, and my experience supports my judgment. Honesty facilitates communication.
A firm, deliberate push is your only answer to the warning. Then, you lift your head, your eyes meeting Ceto's in a stare as steady as stone.
And that's what I want you to know, Ceto. I'm here to find the truth, to resolve this peacefully. We don't have to be adversaries.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I'm a Rancor who forced my way through DisCity's checkpoints. And you think we're on the same side? Would the puppet masters in your ear agree?
If we're talking about sides, my position is neutral. I'm not here to pass judgment. As I said, I believe you have your reasons, and I will ensure you have the chance to state them.
Ceto's gaze cuts with razor-sharp intensity, her presence as imposing as that of the DisCity officials.

Your self-claimed neutrality is also a line for the puppet masters in your ear. In truth, you are maneuvering to secure the most advantageous position for her, ensuring her arguments are properly seen. You will seize every opportunity to make it so.
Let's start with the little girl. You protected her carefully during the fighting. That suggests you meant her no harm. How did you come to be with her?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hardly know her. Found her on the road.
On the road? Records show you have no entry or exit documentation, and your attempt to enter was blocked. Are you saying you found her outside DisCity?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Yes. She was taken out. Your precious city leaks; the wrong people get in, the vulnerable get tossed out. If I hadn't grabbed her, she'd be sold off to some godforsaken corner of WhiteSands by now.
Are you saying... the reason you gave at the border was actually true? You weren't lying, or taking a hostage; you were just trying to take her home?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Why lie? If I wasn't dragging that deadweight, your soldiers never would've caught me. If I wanted to sneak in alone, I wouldn't waste time on theatrics.
Ceto's attitude is far from earnest, but her explanation holds a grim logic. Your experience, however, flags lingering discrepancies that keep you from fully accepting her story.
But if that's true, you weren't trying to illegally enter. There was no need to force the checkpoint and cause that chaos. Why not just tell the customs officer what you're telling me now?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Go ask your trigger-happy guards who point guns first. Maybe you'd sit down for a chat with them. I'm a Rancor wielder, a "combat lunatic" who only knows to swing a blade. I don't have the patience to roll over and take it.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: You know what kind of hell I survived. I'll just kill whoever threatens me!

options: Now isn't the time for stubborn pride.
It's because I've spent time with you that I know...

choices.text: Now isn't the time for stubborn pride.
It's because I've spent time with you that I know...

steps.content: I know you're a soldier, a lighthouse keeper. Your enemies are hundreds of times more vicious than any border guard. Your blade was wielded to tear monsters apart.

Whether you admit it or not, you've stood for DisCity before. With or without the Rancor, you don't start fights without reason; you'd consider it beneath you! ...You're still hiding something from me. I know it.

Her silence is not a surrender, but a fortress. Though her glare sharpens, the flinch in her eyes confirms it—you've found a crack in Ceto's armor. Seizing the opening, you draw out that half-finished report.

I haven't mentioned this yet. Upon returning to DisCity, I filed a report on the lighthouse keepers' achievements. But many still refuse to believe anyone can resist the Rancors' influence... So I've been gathering evidence.

I want to prove that even under severe mental erosion, the lighthouse keepers never lost their humanity. Ceto, you are the last soldier of Lighthouse Seven. Your actions are the most compelling evidence. If you don't want your name to be synonymous with madness, tell me your reasons.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...Are you using the lighthouse keepers' name to threaten me?
I'm doing this because I understand you. I trust you. <color=#fb9259>I want to help</color>.

A chorus of sharp, staticky protests erupts in your earpiece, but you drown them out, your gaze locked with Ceto's. You search her eyes desperately for a glimmer of the bond once forged in the crucible of death.
For a long moment, your words hang in the air, and Ceto's gaze falls. When she finally looks up, her lips twist into something sharp and ambiguous, not a smile, but a blade thinly disguised as one.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Still so stubborn, I see... You really want to know that badly?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Then see for yourself.

Just as you suspected, the restraints could never hold her! In a single, fluid motion, she closes the distance. Her bound hands snap up, her fingers locking around your wrist like a vice. A searing light erupts from the shackles, piercing the space between you—

steps.speaker: Customs Officer A
steps.content: You crossed WhiteSands and made it back with the kid? Damn, she hit the jackpot! If she hadn't run into someone with your skills, she'd never have made it back alive.

steps.speaker: Customs Officer B
steps.content: Yeah, it's really remarkable! Worthy of the Sinner title! Here's your form; registration is complete. Please proceed through the security screening over there, then hand this to the staff at the end.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Security screening? I already passed one at the entrance.

steps.speaker: Customs Officer A
steps.content: That one detects Mania, for Sinner registration. This new one inside is for... oh, Rancors! The higher-ups are cracking down. They say if one Rancor slips through, our heads are on the block!

Ceto faltered momentarily at the words. Fortunately, her hood was pulled low, and her shock passed in a heartbeat. By the time the others glanced her way, she had mastered her expression. She gave the girl's hand a gentle squeeze, making a silent promise that she would handle this.

Their "heroic crossing" immediately drew the officers' attention, their gazes sharp with confusion and impatience. In one fluid motion, Ceto swept the girl into her arms, holding her close, and with feigned nonchalance, strode briskly through the newly set "door."

Instantly, crimson lights strobed, and a piercing alarm shattered the air. The synchronized clack-clack of weapons being loaded echoed sharply through the space. Ceto's eyes swept her surroundings: the dark barrels of every stationed guard were now leveled directly at her and the child in her arms.

steps.speaker: Customs Officer A
steps.content: You... you're a Rancor!

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: So what if I am. I never tried to hide it. I never lied. Everything I told you was true. I'm only here to take this kid home.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: If DisCity doesn't welcome my kind, I won't enter. I'll leave immediately; just take the girl and get her home. You've verified it, right? She's one of yours.

Ceto remained still, her gaze steady as one of the customs officers frantically scrambled behind the protective circle. In a deliberate act of peace, she kept her hands in clear view, the girl held gently in her arms as proof of her benign intent. Her calm was met not with understanding, but with his frantic, hysterical shouting.

steps.speaker: Customs Officer A
steps.content: You think I believe that? You people are maniacs who love to slash and kill! Why would someone like you ever help a little girl?!

steps.speaker: Customs Officer B
steps.content: Well, we shouldn't paint them all with the same brush... I've heard some of those Nirvana Port veterans can be useful in a pinch...

steps.speaker: Customs Officer A
steps.content: You think Corruptors recognize family and loyalty? That's bullshit! They're murderous psychos! When they snap, they don't care who you are; they just slash!

steps.speaker: Customs Officer A
steps.content: Stop standing there like an idiot! Get over here! Are you hoping she'll kill you up close?! For all we know, that kid could be a damned Rancor, too!

Ceto's increasingly threatening gaze failed to resolve the situation, instead provoking the customs officer into more extreme reactions. Forcing herself to suppress her emotions, she turned toward a soldier who was steadily aiming his weapon. Their eyes met, making a silent exchange between two warriors that spoke volumes.

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: We cannot allow the child entry. Our orders are clear: anyone or anything that has contacted Rancors is a major security threat. No one enters without thorough screening. And the screening methods... aren't something a child could take.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: I've done nothing wrong, yet because of a weapon, you label people monsters, lunatics, murderers... Fine. Have it your way.

The standoff had drained all the oxygen from the air. Ceto broke the silence with a cold laugh. Deftly, she swung the girl onto her back and unleashed her Mania. The stalemate shattered, and the defensive perimeter dissolved as the S-Class Sinner burst through their blockade, as effortlessly as a storm petrel cutting through a curtain of rain.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Since that's what you think of me, wouldn't I be letting you down if I didn't solve this the "Rancor way"?! You hypocrites!
[Blade Flashes]

steps.speaker: FAC Captain
steps.content: She's broken through! I'll lead the pursuit! The rest of you, contact MBCC for backup! Highest priority alert!
[Exit Flashback]
Your earpiece buzzes with static and urgent voices, a reality you deliberately push away. Nothing is more important than bearing witness to this memory.

You see the exact moment the insults about the lighthouse keepers hit Ceto. A tremor runs through her, her voice sinking into a guttural range as every muscle in her frame locks solid. A sharp creak from the interrogation chair underscores the immense pressure building within her, a stark contrast to the deceptively calm expression she maintains.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: It's just that simple. I understand your point. But I've seen their true faces, and I've made my choice. Those armored, bulky guys... I didn't know who they were. Their recited laws meant nothing to me. I felt no guilt using force.
I'm sorry about the prejudice you've faced. You have every right to be angry. But by lashing out, by fulfilling their worst expectations, is that the truth you choose for yourself?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...Destruction. Killing. That was my survival. It's what I knew. They weren't wrong about me.
Who decided that's all you are? Isn't protection your true skill? Defending your lighthouse, protecting that little girl—

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Chief, I must insist you stop leading the subject!
The voice in your earpiece turns sharp, the official's patience snapping. The veneer of politeness vanishes, replaced by naked anger as he abandons all pretense.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: No amount of rhetoric can redefine this as some "well-intentioned act of necessity." You cannot change the fact of her tyrannical, uncontrolled disregard for the law! I believe our prepared list of questions will better serve DisCity's security interests.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: We need intelligence on her backers. The more she talks, the better. And we are counting on your shackles' perceptive abilities to uncover... deeper truths. Such as who is truly pulling her strings.

The final seconds of your hard-won leeway drain away. You meet Ceto's gaze, searching for a reprieve, but find only an impassive mask; she has heard the official's demand and offers no objection. Trapped between two immovable forces, you have no choice. With a stiff, reluctant motion, you open the document and begin to read, your voice tight.
...Question: Where did you obtain your Rancor?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: From the lighthouse keepers.
Next question: Were the lighthouse keepers affiliated with DisCorps?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: **** no. The lighthouses had no contact with the outside world until the day the last one went dark.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: In terms of organizational structure, were the lighthouse keepers subordinate to DisCorps?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Tsk... Yes.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Third question—
...Did DisCorps provide you with financial support? No, I object. Isn't this question deliberately leading?

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Isn't the weapon in her hand evidence enough of their support?
You...!

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Continue!

The pointless interrogation drags on, draining the room of all energy. Ceto's patience has frayed to a breaking point, and your voice is now a dull monotone. Finally, you reach the last few questions on the list—
Tests show a fragment from another Rancor is attached to yours. Is this fragment connected to your attack...?!

Your voice dies in your throat as revelation hits. You see the same stunned realization dawn on Ceto, a shared shock that clearly pleases the official. His next question comes softly, but it's preceded by a wave of static that crackles like a serpent's warning, the sound feeling unnervingly slick and moist against your ear.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Why did you stop, Chief? Remember, you are being monitored throughout this process. I advise you not to skip or modify questions based on personal sentiments and judgments.
Did you plan to kidnap the hostage, bring her into DisCity, and use that fragment to corrupt her for an attack? Were these actions ordered by the lighthouse keepers or DisCorps...?!

You hold the fraying threads of your control until the question hangs, complete, in the air. The silence that follows is the sound of your composure breaking. Deliberately, you turn a searing gaze upon the camera, realizing it was a calculated act to keep you in the dark.
What Rancor fragment? I was never informed about this!

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Please remain calm. We only discovered it at the last moment—it was cleverly hidden. Perhaps in this plot to destabilize DisCity using a Rancor, the hostage and the fragment were the actual weapons?

But I filed a complete report on Ceto's identity! Her Rancor's origin is properly documented, along with its limited purpose! This sounds like a predetermined theory. Are you going to condemn a soldier who dedicated her life to DisCity over a single Rancor fragment—

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: This is merely a theory, Chief. But do you have a better explanation for why she hid it? No offense, but our job is to investigate all risks, even those you find absurd.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: I'm sure you recall how she deliberately held the hostage in her arms during the detection scan. Maybe it was to use her own Rancor signature as cover, making us detect only one Rancor, all to blindside us when we least expected it.

The official twists every fact into something sinister, reducing the girl to a mere bomb component. Your shackles tremble with the raw, churning heat of Ceto's emotions, and you fear she is on the verge of splintering. Then you look up. Her expression is a lake of perfect calm, its serene surface giving no hint of the depths below.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Is this the best story you could cook up? Quite the imagination. But like I said, why would I bother with something so complicated while dragging along dead weight? If I wanted to kill my way in, could any of you actually stop me?

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Since you've figured me out, I'll drop the act. Yes, the brat was a decoy. I bought her to lower your guard. If I'd known I'd have to force my way through anyway, I could have saved myself the—

To the watching officials, Ceto's demeanor is unwavering. But through the shackles, you feel what churns beneath her cold exterior: a storm of anger, calculation, and anxiety. She's performing. But why?
You rip the earpiece out, throw it to the floor, and turn off the camera, severing the connection.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Hey! What are you doing?!

Relax. I'm not the one in the crosshairs here. You are. What are you hiding? I can't protect you if I don't know what we're dealing with. What's so important you'd rather take the fall than talk? He can't hear us. So tell me the truth now.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: Tell the truth? To you? Or to the DisCity people with all their "opinions"?
They could resort to more extreme measures against you at any moment. When that happens, you won't even get a chance to explain yourself, and that kid won't be any safer for it.

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: But even if a Rancor tells you the truth, would anyone actually believe it?
I will believe you. And I will make everyone else believe, too. I'll make them "see."

steps.speaker: Ceto
steps.content: ...See?

Yes. Exactly what you're thinking. You won't have to say a word. You won't have to prove a thing. Just give me your trust and let me touch your past. Let me shoulder this for you. I promise I won't betray that trust.

A long, tense silence fills the room. Ceto leans forward, her gaze as dissecting as it was during your first encounter. You hold it, unblinking. An eternity seems to pass before she finally reclines in her chair. No words are spoken, but you know this is her silent consent.

Almost immediately, communication from the officials is restored to the Bureau. This time, it bypasses your earpiece entirely, channeling directly to Nightingale. A moment later, the red eye of the surveillance camera flickers back to life.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: Are you here to offer an explanation? Regarding your unauthorized actions and blatant disregard for instructions, I agree that we need a serious discussion.

Sorry to disappoint, but I won't be apologizing. I've said all I need to on the matter. Going in circles with Ceto is a waste of time. She won't give you the answers you want, and she won't get what she needs.

As long as this trust crisis persists, this deadlock will get us nowhere. The only way through this is with verifiable truth. And for that, I have a proposal. One that serves everyone's interests and is far more efficient.

You rise and cross to the corner, your eyes lifting to confront the camera's sterile curve. You know they're there, watching, waiting for this exact show of defiance. But the thought is a distant one, a fact that no longer holds any power over you. Let them have their moment.
Yes, it's what you're thinking. Experiments have proven that the shackles can resonate with a Rancor. I can use that to explore the wielder's mindscape—to a point.

However, the Mania contamination levels on a Rancor are extremely high. Safe resonance requires the wielder's stability and cooperation. That's why the procedure is officially "not recommended." You don't have the authority to order it.
But if I volunteer and willingly accept all consequences, that changes everything. You question my judgment, but keep me on this case. Isn't this the move you were waiting for?

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: I'm sure I don't know what you mean. We do not involve ourselves in other departments' classified research, nor have we guided your actions in any way. However, city security is our paramount concern. Your proposal does have our attention.

steps.speaker: Official
steps.content: What do you require now?
That Rancor fragment. Your so-called "evidence."
The voice on the line slips back into its ingratiating pleasantness, a clear signal that your strategic dance has entered a new phase.
[Blank Screen]

Against a pristine white backdrop, your consciousness is violently wrenched downward into the depths. All your senses are submerged in a slowly flowing liquid; sound blurs into a dull roar, and images drift like phantoms around you.
Suddenly, quick footsteps shatter the blur. A little girl, clutching something to her chest, dashes past, leaving only a glimpse of her defiant, retreating form.
I don't need help. I can do this myself!
Is this the hostage Ceto was protecting? As you watch the girl disappear into the distance, instinct compels you to give chase.
Mmph...!
Are you alright?!

As if weighed down by the heavy object in her arms, she loses her balance and falls before she can get far. Your heart lurches as you rush to her side, but she simply sits up, stubbornly wiping her face with her sleeve before turning to look at you.
Ceto...?!
You freeze in your tracks, your heart skipping a beat. This girl—struggling with an enormous metal gear—is not the hostage.
You are witnessing Ceto's own story, a memory from her childhood.
